description: Believing T extends U ? X : Y evaluates once on a union T, rather than distributing over each member when T is a naked type parameter.
Believing [T] extends [U] still distributes over a union, rather than checking the union as a whole.
Believing a distributive conditional given never returns a branch type, rather than distributing over zero members and yielding never.
Believing a conditional on a concrete, non-generic type is deferred, rather than resolved immediately to one branch.
Believing extends in a conditional tests identical types, rather than assignability (so a subtype or literal passes).
Believing any extends U ? X : Y picks one branch, rather than producing the union of both branches.
Believing infer can be declared anywhere in a type, rather than only inside the extends clause of a conditional type.
Believing repeated infer positions always give a union, rather than a union for covariant positions and an intersection for contravariant ones.
Believing a failed infer match is a compile error, rather than selecting the false branch.
Believing infer on an overloaded function sees every overload, rather than only the last signature.
Believing a homomorphic mapped type drops optional and readonly, rather than preserving them unless changed.
Believing -? and -readonly leave modifiers untouched, rather than removing optionality and readonly from every property.
Believing -? always strips undefined from the value, rather than only removing the optional flag (under exactOptionalPropertyTypes an explicit undefined stays).
Believing remapping a key to never in a mapped type is an error, rather than dropping that property.
Believing a mapped type over a string-literal union yields a union, rather than an object with one property per member.
Believing a homomorphic mapped type over an array or tuple produces an object, rather than an array or tuple of mapped elements.
Believing a template literal with union placeholders is one string type, rather than the cross product of all combinations.
Believing a template literal with a string placeholder accepts any string, rather than only strings matching the pattern.
Believing infer in a template literal captures greedily, rather than matching the shortest prefix before the next literal text.
Believing template literal unions have no size limit, rather than erroring when the cross product exceeds the compiler cap.
Believing distribution happens for any union passed through an alias, rather than only when the checked type is a naked type parameter.
Believing Exclude and Extract test a union as a whole, rather than each member separately via a distributive conditional.
Believing method parameters are always checked contravariantly, rather than bivariantly for method-syntax declarations.
Believing strictFunctionTypes applies to all function types, rather than only function-type properties and not method-syntax declarations.
Believing a type must declare or extend another to be assignable to it, rather than only needing a compatible structure.
Believing excess property errors apply to every assignment, rather than only to fresh object literals.
Believing a Dog[] cannot be assigned to an Animal[], rather than arrays being covariant (an unsound but allowed assignment).
Believing the implementation signature of an overloaded function is callable, rather than only the overload signatures.
Believing overload order does not matter, rather than the first matching overload being chosen.
Believing satisfies widens the expression to the checked type, rather than keeping its narrower inferred type.
Believing satisfies, a type annotation, and an as assertion behave alike, rather than validating without changing, widening, or overriding the type.
Believing as const only affects strings, rather than making object properties readonly and arrays readonly tuples of literal types.
Believing narrowing works on any shared property, rather than needing a literal-typed discriminant in each member.
Believing a switch over a union is checked for completeness by default, rather than needing a default that assigns the value to never.
Believing narrowing of a mutable variable persists inside a later callback, rather than being reset because the variable may change.
Believing keyof (A | B) lists every key of both, rather than only the keys common to both.
Believing T[K1 | K2] is an error, rather than the union of the property types.
Believing T extends X gives T a default of X, rather than a constraint with no default (an uninferred T becomes its constraint, a default needs = X).
Believing a primitive constraint widens the inferred type, rather than keeping the literal (T extends string infers "a").
Believing recursive conditional types have no depth limit, rather than hitting an instantiation depth error without tail-recursive form.
